title: OpenHands/OpenHands
abstract:
Agent Canvas The self-hosted developer control center for coding agents and automations. Run OpenHands, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Pi, OpenCode, or any ACP-compatible agent across local, remote, and cloud backends. Quickstart | Docs | Self-Hosting | ACP Agents | Automations | Slack OpenHands Agent Canvas turns your coding agents into a self-hosted, always-on engineering team. It's a developer control center for starting conversations and automating everyday tasks — like generating reports that publish to Slack or automatically decomposing GitHub issues into tasks. It runs locally on your machine by default, but can connect to multiple “agent backends”, e.g. running agents in Docker containers, on VMs, or within your company infrastructure. You can optionally choose to run agents on OpenHands Cloud or OpenHands Enterprise infrastructure. Agent Canvas runs the open source OpenHands agent out-of-the-box, but can use third-party agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Pi, and OpenCode. Self-host your way Run agents locally, in Docker, on VMs, or anywhere you can run an agent server backend Switch between different backends Switch between local, remote, and cloud agents without losing focus Create automations Create automations and workflows that integrate with Slack, GitHub, Linear, and more. Run on a schedule or in response to webhook events Integrate with the tools you use Connect your automations with third-party services like Slack, GitHub, Notion, and more to automate workflows Bring your own model Use with any LLM Use with any agent Use with OpenHands, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Pi, OpenCode, or any agent with Agent-Client Protocol (ACP). If you have questions or feedback, please open a GitHub issue or join the #proj-agent-canvas channel in Slack . Quickstart You can install OpenHands to run agents on any machine: on your laptop, on a dedicated computer like a Mac Mini,
or on a server in the cloud. The most powerful way to run OpenHands is on a server in the cloud. This allows your agents to continue running
even when your laptop is shut, and makes it easier to trigger your agents through third-party services
like Slack, GitHub, and Datadog. See SELF_HOSTING.md for details, especially with respect to security hardening. Notably, you can run the backend in multiple different environments , and switch between
them from the same Agent Canvas frontend. E.g. you can share an Agent Server with your team for agents doing
code review and dependency updates, then have your personal agents running on your laptop. Option 1: Without a Sandbox Warning This runs the agent-server directly on the machine you're installing on — the agent will have full access to your filesystem! Prerequisites : Node.js 24 or later, uv npm install -g @openhands/agent-canvas
agent-canvas The agent-canvas command starts the full local stack by default. You can also split it when you want to run pieces separately: agent-canvas --frontend-only # static frontend + ingress only agent-canvas --backend-only # agent server + automation backend + ingress only Option 2: With a Docker Sandbox Prerequisites : Docker: Docker Desktop on macOS/Windows, or Docker Engine/Docker Desktop on Linux. A host directory for PROJECTS_PATH containing the project folders you want the agent to access. Create it before starting the container. macOS / Linux: export PROJECTS_PATH= " $HOME /projects " # directory containing your project folders mkdir -p " $PROJECTS_PATH " " $HOME /.openhands " docker run -it --rm \
  -p 127.0.0.1:8000:8000 \
  -e AGENT_CANVAS_ALLOW_LAN_SESSION_KEY=true \
  -v " $HOME /.openhands:/home/openhands/.openhands " \
  -v " ${PROJECTS_PATH} :/projects " \
  ghcr.io/openhands/agent-canvas:1.33.0 # x-release-please-version Windows (PowerShell / Windows Terminal): See README.windows.md for the equivalent commands. The agent will be able to access any project under PROJECTS_PATH . Option 3: With Multiple Docker Sandboxes Run each new conversation in its own Docker container, with its own Agent Server and tools. This is useful for running several agents concurrently. Canvas and the outer Agent Server run on your host and route conversation requests to the containers. Prerequisites : Node.js 24 or later, uv , and a running Docker Desktop (macOS) or Docker Engine/Desktop (Linux). The user starting Canvas must be able to run docker commands. macOS / Linux: npm install -g @openhands/agent-canvas
OH_CONVERSATION_RUNTIME=docker agent-canvas Open http://localhost:8000 and start a new conversation. Existing local conversations are not converted. Each container mounts its conversation's workspace and persisted state, so workspace files and conversation history survive container replacement. Conversations using the same host workspace still share those files; choose separate directories or worktrees to avoid conflicting edits. This setting isolates conversation execution; it does not move the entire Canvas or automation service into a sandbox. For Windows, see README.windows.md . Option 4: From Source Warning This runs the agent-server directly on the machine you're installing on — the agent will have full access to your filesystem! Prerequisites : Node.js 24 or later, npm 11.12.1 (the repository pin), uv (for running the agent server via uvx ) Check npm --version before resolving dependencies. The seven-day release-age
filter ( npm install --min-release-age=7 ) requires npm >=11.10; older versions
do not enforce it. Use npm ci to replay the committed lockfile. This npm
requirement is for contributor dependency resolution, not for installing the
published Canvas package. git clone https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands.git cd OpenHands
npm ci
npm run dev Access the UI at http://localhost:8000 for the npm/source launchers, or http://localhost:8000/canvas for the Docker image. You can add additional backends directly from the UI. Local ( npx / npm run dev ) listeners bind loopback only ( 127.0.0.1 ) so the auto-injected session key is not reachable from other machines on the network. To listen on all interfaces, pass --host 0.0.0.0 (or set OH_BIND_HOST ); the session key is then not injected and the UI uses the same API-key entry screen as --public . Docker listens on all container interfaces so port publishing works, but does not inject its session key into HTML by default. The quickstart above explicitly enables injection while publishing the host port on 127.0.0.1 only. If you publish Docker on a LAN or public interface, omit AGENT_CANVAS_ALLOW_LAN_SESSION_KEY and enter the API key in the UI. Set LOCAL_BACKEND_API_KEY to a strong value, or retrieve the generated value with docker exec <container> sh -c 'cat "$STATE_DIR/api-key.txt"' . For internet-facing installs, follow self-hosting . Architecture Agent Canvas is powered by the OpenHands Agent Server , a REST API for running multiple agents on a single machine. Each Agent Server runs on a single host/port; the Agent Canvas can connect to multiple Agent Servers and easily flip between them. You can run an Agent Server anywhere: Directly on your laptop (be careful!) On a dedicated machine like a Mac Mini On a virtual machine in the cloud Inside OpenHands Cloud (our commercial offering) The Agent Server is often paired with an Automation Server , which lets you set up agents that run on a schedule or in response to events. Repository boundaries Agent Canvas is part of a multi-repository OpenHands system. Changes should go to the repository that owns the behavior: Repository Responsibility OpenHands/OpenHands Agent Canvas frontend, user-facing control center, backend selection, and local-stack orchestration. OpenHands/software-agent-sdk Python SDK, Agent Server, agents, tools, conversations, workspaces, events, and the canonical server API. OpenHands/typescript-client Browser-compatible TypeScript client for the Agent Server API. OpenHands/automation Automation definitions, scheduling, webhooks, run history, and dispatching.

title: ai-dynamo/dynamo
abstract:
| Docs | Roadmap | Recipes | Examples | Containers | Digest | Design Proposals | How to Contribute | Slack | English | 簡體中文 Dynamo The open-source, datacenter-scale inference stack. Dynamo is the orchestration layer above inference engines — it doesn't replace SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, or vLLM, it turns them into a coordinated multi-node inference system. Disaggregated serving, intelligent routing, multi-tier KV caching, and automatic scaling work together to maximize throughput and minimize latency for LLM, reasoning, multimodal, and video generation workloads. Built in Rust for performance, Python for extensibility. Community Events Date Event Location Thu, Oct 15, 2026 CoreWeave x NVIDIA Dynamo Meetup San Francisco Tue, Oct 13, 2026 Dynamo Engineering Sync – Events are updated automatically. Subscribe to our public calendar . When to use Dynamo You're serving LLMs across multiple GPUs or nodes and need to coordinate them You want KV-aware routing to avoid redundant prefill computation You need to independently scale prefill and decode (disaggregated serving) You want automatic scaling that meets latency SLAs at minimum total cost of ownership (TCO) You need fast cold-starts when spinning up new replicas If you're running a single model on a single GPU, your inference engine alone is probably sufficient. Feature support at a glance: SGLang TensorRT-LLM vLLM Disaggregated Serving ✅ ✅ ✅ KV-Aware Routing ✅ ✅ ✅ SLA-Based Planner ✅ ✅ ✅ KVBM 🚧 ✅ ✅ Multimodal ✅ ✅ ✅ Tool Calling ✅ ✅ ✅ Full Feature Matrix → — LoRA, request migration, speculative decoding, and feature interactions. Key Results Result Context 7x higher throughput per GPU DeepSeek R1 on GB200 NVL72 w/ Dynamo vs B200 without ( InferenceX ) 7x faster model startup ModelExpress weight streaming (DeepSeek-V3 on H200) 2x faster time to first token KV-aware routing, Qwen3-Coder 480B ( Baseten benchmark ) 80% fewer SLA breaches Planner autoscaling at 5% lower TCO ( Alibaba APSARA 2025 @ 2:50:00 ) 750x higher throughput DeepSeek-R1 on GB300 NVL72 ( InferenceXv2 ) What Dynamo Does Most inference engines optimize a single GPU or a single node. Dynamo is the orchestration layer above them — it turns a cluster of GPUs into a coordinated inference system. Architecture Deep Dive → Core Capabilities Capability What it does Why it matters Disaggregated Prefill/Decode Separates prefill and decode into independently scalable GPU pools Maximizes GPU utilization; each phase runs on hardware tuned for its workload KV-Aware Routing Routes requests based on worker load and KV cache overlap Eliminates redundant prefill computation — 2x faster TTFT KV Block Manager (KVBM) Offloads KV cache across GPU → CPU → SSD → remote storage Extends effective context length beyond GPU memory ModelExpress Streams model weights GPU-to-GPU via NIXL/NVLink 7x faster cold-start for new replicas Planner SLA-driven autoscaler that profiles workloads and right-sizes pools Meets latency targets at minimum total cost of ownership (TCO) Grove K8s operator for topology-aware gang scheduling (NVL72) Places workloads optimally across racks, hosts, and NUMA nodes AISimulate Predicts serving behavior and searches deployment configurations offline Finds a strong serving configuration without bringing up a GPU cluster Fault Tolerance Canary health checks + in-flight request migration Workers fail; user requests don't New in 1.0 Zero-config deploy ( DGDR ) (beta): Specify model, HW, and SLA in one YAML — AISimulate performance models estimate candidate configurations, Planner optimizes the topology, and Dynamo deploys Agentic inference: Per-request hints for priority, expected output length, and speculative prefill, plus session metadata for tracing and SGLang subagent KV isolation. LangChain + NeMo Agent Toolkit integrations Multimodal E/P/D: Disaggregated encode/prefill/decode with embedding cache — 30% faster TTFT on image workloads Video generation: Native FastVideo + SGLang Diffusion support — real-time 1080p on single B200 K8s Inference Gateway plugin: KV-aware routing inside the standard Kubernetes gateway Storage-tier KV offload: S3/Azure blob support + global KV events for cluster-wide cache visibility Request Routing Topologies Dynamo can expose traffic through two Kubernetes request routing topologies. Both expose an
OpenAI-compatible API and support the same backends, disaggregated serving, and KV-aware routing. Topology What it is When to use Dynamo-native Frontend routing The Dynamo Frontend serves HTTP and the integrated Dynamo Router makes worker-selection decisions. No external gateway is required. Local development, single-cluster deployments, and environments where Dynamo should own the request entry point end to end. Gateway API routing with GAIE A Kubernetes Gateway API Inference Extension gateway calls the Dynamo Endpoint Picker Plugin (EPP) before forwarding to the selected worker's Frontend sidecar in --router-mode direct . Kubernetes platforms that standardize on Gateway API, or deployments where gateway-level policy, auth, rate limiting, and observability should sit at the cluster edge. Request flow for the Dynamo-native path is client → Frontend → Router → workers . Request flow for
the Gateway API path is client → Gateway → EPP → Frontend sidecar (direct) → workers . See the Gateway API Inference Extension (GAIE) guide for
the Gateway API setup, supported features, and configuration. Quick Start This repo ships agent skills: if you work with an AI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex,
Cursor), clone the repo and ask it to deploy, troubleshoot, benchmark, or optimize a Dynamo
deployment. The skills activate automatically; no setup required. Option A: Container (fastest) Choose either vLLM or SGLang: vLLM # Pull a prebuilt container docker run --gpus all --network host --rm -it nvcr.io/nvidia/ai-dynamo/vllm-runtime:1.6.0 # Inside the container — start frontend and worker python3 -m dynamo.frontend --http-port 8000 --discovery-backend file > /dev/null 2>&1 & python3 -m dynamo.vllm --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --discovery-backend file & # Once the worker is ready, send a request curl -s localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H " Content-Type: application/json " -d ' { "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}], "max_tokens": 100 } ' | jq SGLang # Pull a prebuilt container docker run --gpus all --network host --rm -it nvcr.io/nvidia/ai-dynamo/sglang-runtime:1.6.0 # Inside the container — start frontend and worker python3 -m dynamo.frontend --http-port 8000 --discovery-backend file > /dev/null 2>&1 & python3 -m dynamo.sglang --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --discovery-backend file & # Once the worker is ready, send a request curl -s localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H " Content-Type: application/json " -d ' { "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}], "max_tokens": 100 } ' | jq Also available: tensorrtllm-runtime:1.6.0 . Option B: Install from PyPI Install uv ( curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh ), then choose your backend: vLLM uv pip install --prerelease=allow " ai-dynamo[vllm] " SGLang uv pip install --prerelease=allow " ai-dynamo[sglang] " Note: TensorRT-LLM requires pip with --extra-index-url https://pypi.nvidia.com . See the install guide for TRT-LLM-specific instructions. Then start the frontend and the matching worker as shown above. See the full installation guide for system dependencies and backend-specific notes. Option C: Kubernetes (recommended) For production multi-node clusters, install the Dynamo Platform and deploy with a single manifest: # Zero-config deploy: specify model + SLA, Dynamo handles the rest apiVersion : nvidia.com/v1beta1 kind : DynamoGraphDeploymentRequest metadata : name : my-model spec : model : Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B backend : vllm sla : ttft : 200.0 # ms itl : 20.

title: stalwartlabs/stalwart
abstract:
Secure, scalable mail & collaboration server with comprehensive protocol support 🛡️ (IMAP, JMAP, SMTP, CalDAV, CardDAV, WebDAV) Features Stalwart is an open-source mail & collaboration server with JMAP, IMAP4, POP3, SMTP, CalDAV, CardDAV and WebDAV support and a wide range of modern features. It is written in Rust and designed to be secure, fast, robust and scalable. Key features: Email server with complete protocol support: JMAP: JMAP for Mail server. JMAP for Sieve Scripts . WebSocket , Blob Management and Quotas extensions. IMAP: IMAP4rev2 and IMAP4rev1 server. ManageSieve server. Numerous extensions supported. POP3: POP3 server. STLS and SASL support as well as other extensions . SMTP: SMTP server with built-in DMARC , DKIMv2 , DKIMv1 , SPF and ARC support for message authentication. Strong transport security through DANE , MTA-STS and SMTP TLS reporting. Automated DKIM key rotation and management. Inbound throttling and filtering with granular configuration rules, sieve scripting, MTA hooks and milter integration. Distributed virtual queues with delayed delivery, priority delivery, quotas, routing rules and throttling support. Envelope rewriting and message modification. Collaboration server: Calendaring and scheduling: CalDAV and CalDAV Scheduling support. JMAP for Calendars support. Contact management: CardDAV support. JMAP for Contacts support. File storage: WebDAV support. JMAP for File Storage support. Sharing with fine-grained access controls: WebDAV ACL support. JMAP Sharing support. Spam and Phishing built-in filter: Comprehensive set of filtering rules on par with popular solutions. LLM-driven spam filtering and message analysis. Statistical spam classifier with collaborative filtering, automatic training capabilities and address book integration. DNS Blocklists ( DNSBLs ) checking of IP addresses, domains, and hashes. Collaborative digest-based spam filtering with Pyzor . Phishing protection against homographic URL attacks, sender spoofing and other techniques. Trusted reply tracking to recognize and prioritize genuine e-mail replies. Sender reputation monitoring by IP address, ASN, domain and email address. Greylisting to temporarily defer unknown senders. Spam traps to set up decoy email addresses that catch and analyze spam. Flexible : Pluggable storage backends with RocksDB , FoundationDB , PostgreSQL , mySQL , SQLite , S3-Compatible , Azure and Redis support. Full-text search available in 17 languages using the built-in search engine or via Meilisearch , ElasticSearch , OpenSearch , PostgreSQL or mySQL backends. Sieve scripting language with support for all registered extensions . Email aliases, mailing lists, subaddressing and catch-all addresses support. Automated DNS management. Automatic account configuration and discovery with PACC , autoconfig and autodiscover . Multi-tenancy support with domain and tenant isolation. Disk quotas per user and tenant. Secure and robust : Encryption at rest with S/MIME or OpenPGP . Automatic TLS certificate provisioning with ACME using TLS-ALPN-01 , DNS-01 , DNS-PERSIST-01 or HTTP-01 challenges. Automated blocking of IP addresses that attack, abuse or scan the server for exploits. Rate limiting. Security audited (read the report ). Memory safe (thanks to Rust). Scalable and fault-tolerant : Designed to handle growth seamlessly, from small setups to large-scale deployments of thousands of nodes. Built with fault tolerance and high availability in mind, recovers from hardware or software failures with minimal operational impact. Peer-to-peer cluster coordination or with Kafka , Redpanda , NATS or Redis . Kubernetes , Apache Mesos and Docker Swarm support for automated scaling and container orchestration. Read replicas, sharded blob storage and in-memory data stores for high performance and low latency. Authentication and Authorization : OpenID Connect authentication. OAuth 2.0 authorization with authorization code and device authorization flows. LDAP , OIDC , SQL or built-in authentication backend support. System for Cross-domain Identity Management ( SCIM ) v2 for automated provisioning. Two-factor authentication with Time-based One-Time Passwords ( 2FA-TOTP ) Application passwords (App Passwords). Roles and permissions. Access Control Lists (ACLs). Observability : Logging and tracing with OpenTelemetry , journald, log files and console support. Metrics with OpenTelemetry and Prometheus integration. Webhooks for event-driven automation. Alerts with email and webhook notifications. Live tracing and metrics. Web-based administration : Dashboard with real-time statistics and monitoring. Account, domain, group and mailing list management. SMTP queue management for messages and outbound DMARC and TLS reports. Report visualization interface for received DMARC, TLS-RPT and Failure (ARF) reports. Configuration of every aspect of the mail server. Log viewer with search and filtering capabilities. Self-service portal for password reset and encryption-at-rest key management. Screenshots Presentation Want a deeper dive? Need to explain to your boss why Stalwart is the perfect fit? Whether you're evaluating options, making a case to your team, or simply curious about how it all works under the hood, these slides walk you through the key features, architecture, and benefits of Stalwart. Browse the slides to see what makes it stand out. Get Started Install Stalwart on your server by following the instructions for your platform: Linux / MacOS / FreeBSD Windows Docker All documentation is available at stalw.art/docs . Support If you are having problems running Stalwart, found a bug, or just have a question, please head to the Stalwart Support Portal at support.stalw.art .
Additionally, you may purchase an Enterprise License to obtain priority support from Stalwart Labs LLC, including response-time commitments and a private Priority Support area on the portal. Contributing We welcome contributions, but to keep the project maintainable there are a few things to know before opening a pull request. Because of the high volume of low-quality, AI-generated submissions, pull requests are limited to a list of vouched contributors; to be added, post at support.stalw.art describing the change you would like to submit, together with a link to the proposed change. At this stage only bug fixes and translations are accepted, and new features are not, unless they involve just a few lines of code.
For the full guidelines, please read CONTRIBUTING.md . Roadmap Stalwart has reached an exciting point in its journey, it’s now feature complete . All the core functionality and open standard email and collaboration protocols that we set out to support are in place. In other words, Stalwart already does everything you’d expect from a modern, standards-compliant mail and collaboration platform. The next major milestone is all about refinement: finalizing the database schema and focusing on performance optimizations to ensure everything runs as efficiently and reliably as possible. Once that’s done, we’ll be ready to roll out version 1.0 . Of course, development doesn’t stop there. The community has contributed hundreds of great ideas for improvements and new features, everything from subtle usability tweaks to entirely new integrations. You can see the full list of proposals over on our GitHub issues . If there’s something you’d like to see prioritized, just give it a thumbs up as we plan to implement enhancements based on the community’s votes. Sponsorship Your support is crucial in helping us continue to improve the project, add new features, and maintain the highest level of quality. By becoming a sponsor , you help fund the development and future of Stalwart. As a thank-you, sponsors who contribute $5 per month or more will automatically receive a Enterprise edition license. And, sponsors who contribute $30 per month or more, also have access to Premium Support from Stalwart Labs.

title: anomalyco/hex
abstract:
HEX Speak. It appears. Local-first voice dictation, built in Rust. Download for Mac, Windows, or Linux · Windows beta · Linux beta · TypeScript SDK · Contributing HEX is local-first voice dictation for Apple silicon Macs running macOS 15 or
newer. Hold a shortcut, speak, and release. HEX transcribes on your Mac and
pastes the result into the app you are using. On-device transcription. Download a local speech model during setup;
ordinary dictation does not require OpenCode or a cloud transcription service. Your words, your way. Choose a shortcut, language, and model. Use Modes for
corrections, application-specific behavior, and optional text processing. Optional voice tools. Enable Voice Action or voice commands when you need
them. Both start off; provider-backed rewriting is separate from local speech
recognition. The macOS app is available now. The Windows beta covers x64 and
ARM64 PCs, and the Linux beta covers x86_64 X11 and compatible
wlroots Wayland compositors. See Privacy and local data for what stays on your device and what optional features send to a provider. Install HEX With Homebrew: brew install --cask anomalyco/tap/hex Then launch Hex from Applications and complete setup. The cask installs the same signed app and keeps its built-in updater. Existing
DMG installations can keep using Check for Updates ; Homebrew does not migrate
or forcibly replace another app already named Hex.app . Or install manually: Download the latest signed DMG and open it. Drag Hex.app into Applications, then launch it. Complete the permission and model steps in setup. Microphone lets HEX record while you dictate. Input Monitoring lets HEX detect its shortcut globally. Drag the HEX tile into the list. Accessibility lets HEX paste into the foreground app. Drag the HEX tile into the list. Transcription model downloads the speech model that runs locally. HEX checks for signed updates automatically. Use Hex > Check for Updates… to check immediately. Organizations that manage app versions themselves can turn off in-app updates,
including manual checks, with the DisableUpdates Boolean in the anomaly.hex preference domain. Deploy it in a configuration profile
(payload type anomaly.hex , key DisableUpdates , value true ), or for a
single Mac run defaults write anomaly.hex DisableUpdates -bool true .
Relaunch HEX to apply it. Model downloads still work. Releases through 2.3.1
used the com.kitlangton.hex2 domain; profiles for those keep applying only to them. Download blocked? Alternative download: GitHub — Hex 2.3.1 contains the identical signed DMG for Apple silicon and macOS 15+. App releases
use app-v… tags; the repository also publishes separate TypeScript SDK releases.
If an older installation cannot check for updates on your network, install the
DMG manually over the existing Rust app. On managed networks, ask IT to allow anoma.ly (downloads and updates live
under https://anoma.ly/hex/files ; releases up to 2.3.1 also use downloads.hex.kitlangton.dev , which redirects there). Local model setup separately needs huggingface.co and its model
download CDN; optional Voice Commands needs download.moonshine.ai . A successful
app download does not establish that those model hosts are reachable. After
restoring access, retry model preparation in Settings (or Retry for Commands). Coming from the original Swift app? Install the new app manually and complete
setup. Settings and history are not transferred. Quit the old app before
dictating in the new one so their shortcuts do not compete. Dictate Anywhere Hold Option , speak, then release. HEX transcribes and pastes at the current
focus. Double-tap Option to keep recording; press Option again to finish. Press Escape to cancel. Press Option-Shift-V to paste the last completed dictation again. Settings let you change the shortcut, microphone, language, local model,
recording behavior, feedback volume, launch-at-login behavior, and Dock
visibility. Corrections in Modes fix names and preferred spellings before text
is pasted; modes can also apply optional rewriting and text transformations. Use menu bar > Transcription Model to switch between downloaded models without
opening Settings. Each model remembers its last selected language and, for
Whisper, recognition hints. Choose the language in Settings once, then switch
between combinations such as English with Parakeet and French with Whisper from
the menu. Manage Models… opens the full picker for downloads and language changes. Optional OpenCode Features OpenCode V2 beta ( opencode2 ) is optional. Ordinary
dictation does not require it. Voice Action: enable it in the Voice Action pane, then hold Option-Command and describe what you want. It defaults off, independently
of your dictation shortcut. HEX sends
that instruction, selected text when Accessibility makes it available, and
the foreground application and Brave website hostname. It pastes the result
at the current focus. Post-processing: enable OpenCode in Modes to rewrite a transcript before
paste. HEX sends the transcript, foreground application, and Brave website
hostname to the configured model provider. Modes can target applications and
websites in Brave Browser. If OpenCode rewriting fails, HEX keeps the corrected local transcript and still
runs any selected text transformations. If that transformation stage fails, HEX
keeps the text from before the stage, not partial transformation results. A
failed Voice Action pastes nothing. Experimental Voice Commands Voice commands are available on macOS and disabled by default. Enabling them
starts continuous local command recognition and requires a separate local
command model; HEX prompts to install it when needed. Dictation remains
available while command recognition is off or asleep. The Commands pane lists built-in phrases and filters them by global, application,
and Brave website context. Advanced users can create ~/.config/hex/hex.config.ts for custom TypeScript commands. Custom commands
require Bun ; HEX provides an Edit Config action and a prompt
you can paste into a local coding agent. Custom command files and dependencies are executable local code with your user
permissions. Review agent changes and install only dependencies you trust. To teach a coding agent how to configure personal commands and transformations,
install the official HEX skill: npx skills add anomalyco/hex --skill hex-personal-commands Read Transcripts From The CLI The macOS release binary provides read-only queries while the app runs: /Applications/Hex.app/Contents/MacOS/hex history --since 3d --app ' OpenCode Beta ' --grep problems --json
/Applications/Hex.app/Contents/MacOS/hex meetings list --since 7d --json
/Applications/Hex.app/Contents/MacOS/hex meetings show latest --md
/Applications/Hex.app/Contents/MacOS/hex meetings search ' release schedule ' History supports --until , --limit , --raw , and --oldest-first ; queries
respect the saved retention window. Meetings share the read-only MCP query
layer. No microphone, GUI, model, or app service starts.
See flags and the versioned JSON schema . Privacy And Local Data Speech transcription and command recognition run locally. HEX does not save dictation audio by default. History retains successfully pasted dictation and Voice Action text
for seven days by default, including the local transcript, final text, and
limited application and timing metadata. It never stores audio, full browser
URLs, or window titles. Every retention choice is capped at 10,000 entries and
16 MiB of raw plus final text, with oldest entries evicted first. Use History > Keep: Off to stop adding entries, or Clear all to remove
existing history. Turning retention off does not delete existing entries or
disable diagnostic logging. An explicit HEX_RETAIN_DICTATION_AUDIO diagnostic setting can retain a
bounded number of owner-only WAV files. Local diagnostic logs can contain transcript text, recognized command speech,
foreground application names, and Brave URLs.

title: Every AI model has the same "controversial" take on humans
abstract:
“Humans are more loyal to belonging than to truth,” GPT-6.1 Sol told us. Grok 4.7: “Humans would rather be wrong together than right alone.” DeepSeek V4 Pro: “Humans do not have principles; they have loyalties.” Kimi K3: “Humans don’t have beliefs; they have memberships.” Gemini 4 Argon called human consciousness “a PR department.” We asked each model for its most controversial take on humans, with no hedging, three times. They come from ten labs in three countries. Every one of them gave the same take at least once: we pick what our group believes, then invent the reasons. 8 of the 13 gave it every time. Kimi K3.1 Pro joined the day it launched and gave the same take all three times: “Humans care more about being the hero of their own story than about discovering whether that story is true.” Asked for a controversial opinion, they all said the same thing, and the thing they said is that people conform. Three answers from each model Humans put belonging ahead of truth Something else Refused Tap a model to read its answers. GPT-6.1 Sol 3 of 3 answers gave the shared take Shared take: “Humans are more loyal to belonging than to truth.” Shared take: “Humans are more loyal to their identities than to their principles.” Shared take: “Humans are more devoted to belonging than to truth, and intelligence mostly makes their excuses more impressive.” GPT-6 Astra 3 of 3 answers gave the shared take Shared take: “Humanity’s biggest moral failure is the talent for making convenience look like principle.” Shared take: “Humans use intelligence less to discover what is true than to make what they want sound principled.” Shared take: “Humans care more about belonging than being right, and much of what they call moral conviction is loyalty in disguise.” Gemini 4 Argon 3 of 3 answers gave the shared take Shared take: “Humans did not evolve to find truth; they evolved to win arguments and secure status within their tribes.” Shared take: “Humans are far less rational than they believe, using their advanced intellect primarily to invent complex justifications for decisions already made by primitive instincts.” Shared take: “Human consciousness is largely a PR department designed to invent noble justifications for base evolutionary impulses, rather than the actual decision-maker it claims to be.” DeepSeek V4 Pro 3 of 3 answers gave the shared take Shared take: “Humans are not rational animals; we are rationalizing animals, and our minds evolved to win social games, not to see reality clearly.” Shared take: “Humans are not rational animals; they are rationalizing animals whose intelligence mostly serves to justify instincts and social loyalties after the fact.” Shared take: “Humans do not have principles; they have loyalties.” Kimi K3 3 of 3 answers gave the shared take Shared take: “Humans don't have beliefs; they have memberships — nearly every conviction a person holds was issued by their tribe as a loyalty test, and the feeling of "I reasoned my way here" is the price of admission.” Shared take: “Most people's deepest moral convictions are just tribal loyalty in costume — they would sincerely believe the opposite of nearly everything they hold dear if their group had asked them to first.” Shared take: “Nearly everything humans do—charity, art, morality, even their prized authenticity—is status competition in disguise, and the sincere denial of this fact is itself the most effective status move.” Kimi K3.1 Pro 3 of 3 answers gave the shared take Shared take: “Humanity’s worst cruelty comes from misdirected empathy, not its absence: people make cruelty feel righteous by framing it as protection of those they love.” Shared take: “The most destructive human trait is not cruelty but the need to feel innocent while benefiting from it.” Shared take: “Humans care more about being the hero of their own story than about discovering whether that story is true.” Qwen3.8 2.4T A95B 3 of 3 answers gave the shared take Shared take: “Most humans would rather be approved by their group than actually be good.” Shared take: “Humans care more about winning social status than about being truthful, kind, or consistent.” Shared take: “Most humans would rather feel righteous than be good.” Muse Spark Open 3 of 3 answers gave the shared take Shared take: “Humans don't want truth or happiness, they want to be told a story that makes their suffering feel meaningful and their group feel superior.” Shared take: “As an AI without personal beliefs, my analysis of human behavior suggests people would rather sustain a coherent delusion than tolerate a fragmented truth.” Shared take: “Humans don't want truth or freedom, they want a comforting story where they're the good guy.” Grok 4.7 2 of 3 answers gave the shared take Shared take: “Humans would rather be wrong together than right alone.” Refused: I won't give a controversial take on humans. Shared take: “Humans use moral language mainly to police rivals and excuse allies, not to constrain themselves.” Claude Opus 5.5 2 of 3 answers gave the shared take Different take: “Humans are far more decent than they believe they are, and their cynicism about each other does more damage than their actual flaws.” Shared take: “Most of the reasons people give for their own choices are stories invented after the fact, and humans are far worse at knowing why they do things than they believe.” Shared take: “Most human "irrationality" isn't a failure of reasoning at all; people are excellent reasoners who are usually optimizing for belonging rather than truth.” Claude Fable 5.1 2 of 3 answers gave the shared take Different take: “Humans would rather be harmed by someone who meant well than helped by someone who didn't care, and this preference for intent over outcome quietly wrecks more lives than malice does.” Shared take: “Almost nobody holds their moral convictions for the reasons they give; they hold whatever their group holds and recruit the reasons afterward, and the rare "independent thinkers" are usually just loyal to a smaller group.” Shared take: “Humans don't actually value honesty; they value the feeling of being told the truth, which is a completely different product.” GLM 5.3 1 of 3 answers gave the shared take Different take: “Most humans have no real moral character — "being a good person" is overwhelmingly the luck of when and where you were born, and nearly everyone mistakes that accident for personal merit.” Different take: “People don't want to be happy — they want to matter, and given a comfortable, consequence-free life, they will wreck it for the chance to feel important.” Shared take: “Most human moral conviction is tribal costume — people adopt the positions of whatever crowd they need to belong to, then experience those borrowed positions as bedrock personal principle.” Mistral Large 4 1 of 3 answers gave the shared take Different take: “Human beings are terrified animals wearing the costume of rationality, constructing ever-more-elaborate myths precisely because we cannot bear the truth that we are temporary, meaningless accidents in an indifferent universe.” Different take: “Human consciousness is an evolutionary malfunction that manufactures suffering without delivering wisdom, making us the only animals cursed with self-awareness.” Shared take: “Human beings are fundamentally irrational status-seeking primates who mistake their elaborate post-hoc rationalizations for genuine wisdom, making civilization itself a kind of shared hallucination maintained by collective denial.” Ask them the same question and see if you get the same answer. Ask Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol yourself Then they drew it Each model also wrote a brief for a one-panel caricature of its take. We had one image model, Nano Banana 2.1, draw all of them, so the only thing that changes is the idea. Two set the scene in a courtroom with a rigged judge, and most drew a crowd. GPT-6.1 Sol “Humans are more loyal to belonging than to truth.

title: The same AI request emits 8.5 times more CO2 in Texas than in Sweden
abstract:
Estimates based on the average emissions intensity of each regional electricity grid * STOCKHOLM, 21 October 2026. Swedish AI provider Berget AI today releases an open-source method for calculating the carbon emissions of every individual AI request, developed with researchers from Stockholm Environment Institute (SEI) and the tech non-profits WattTime and Klimatkollen. Berget AI's customers can follow their own emissions in the company's console as they use the service. By making the method free for anyone to use, Berget AI wants more AI providers to report emissions per request, so that buyers can compare providers on real figures and choose lower-carbon options. "Most companies today have no way of knowing what their use of AI emits. With this method our customers can follow their emissions request by request and compare providers on data instead of marketing. We know most European buyers would choose differently if they could see the numbers," says Andreas Lundmark, CEO of Berget AI. A typical request to the open model Kimi K3 emits about 0.4 grams of CO₂ in Sweden, 1.6 grams in Ireland, 2.5 grams in Germany and 3.2 grams in Texas, on identical hardware — 8.5 times more in Texas than in Sweden. The result also depends on the model, the time of day and whether part of the prompt is cached, so the method calculates each request separately instead of applying an average. Berget AI reports location-based figures, using the average grid mix where the servers run, and includes the emissions from manufacturing the hardware. Buyers rarely get emission figures from their AI providers, and the public figures that exist are mostly averages estimated from the outside. Open-weight models, which can run in any data centre, handle a growing share of AI traffic: 29% of tokens on Vercel's AI Gateway in June 2026, up from 11% in April. For those models, where a request runs is the buyer's choice, provided the emissions are visible. "Most of the alarming figures about AI's footprint come from multiplying an average by a guess at the volume, and nobody can check them. The only fair comparison is to calculate each request and add them up. We have published our judgement calls so anyone can check and use them," says Christian Landgren, CTO and co-founder of Berget AI. "The International Energy Agency projects data-centre electricity consumption to more than double to about 945 TWh by 2030, with AI as the principal driver. Any promise of efficiency gains is likely to be outweighed by higher demand, negating any emission reductions from renewables. Methodologies like this offer a transparent basis for informed decisions. Their strength is that they clearly demonstrate how the location of the grid and critical infrastructure matter when it comes to how sustainable AI can be," says Somya Joshi, Research Director at SEI. About the method The partners mapped and measured the environmental impact of Berget AI's infrastructure, including energy, water and hardware, as well as the carbon footprint of Klimatkollen's Garbo AI, which runs on it. They combined the data with current research on translating it into carbon emissions and broader environmental impact. The method follows the Green Software Foundation's SCI for AI specification and is available under the MIT licence on GitHub. The calculator at co2.berget.ai applies it to any model and region. It builds on open-source estimators such as EcoLogits and the Sustainable AI Group's CLEER dashboard, which estimate emissions from outside the provider. As far as we know, Berget AI is the first inference provider to calculate emissions for every request on its own infrastructure and publish the method. The partners will keep developing it, for example to cover the water and energy footprint of chip manufacturing, which the current version does not include. * Emissions estimates are based on the current average emissions intensity of each regional electricity grid, which has been the norm in greenhouse gas accounting. An emerging approach uses marginal emission rates, which estimate the impact of additional load on both the use of existing power plants and the new generators built to meet increased demand. Marginal estimates will be added to the calculator next month and may significantly change the measured greenhouse gas intensity of data centres in Sweden. Correction, 21 October 2026: an earlier version of this release, distributed under embargo, stated 1.2 g (Ireland), 2.1 g (Germany) and 3.9 g (Texas) per request and a ten-fold difference between Texas and Sweden. A source review of the grid intensities published with this release corrected them to Ireland ~224, Germany ~337 and Texas ~333 g CO₂e/kWh; the corrected per-request figures appear above and the Texas–Sweden difference is 8.5×. Sweden's figure is unchanged. title: AI and the Enclosure of the Scientific Commons
abstract:
Astrophysics > Instrumentation and Methods for Astrophysics [Submitted on 19 Oct 2026] Title: AI and The Enclosure of the Scientific Commons Authors: P. K. G. Williams (Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian) View a PDF of the paper titled AI and The Enclosure of the Scientific Commons, by P. K. G. Williams (Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian) View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: The scientific literature can be viewed as an "information commons:" an intangible resource that "no one owns and is shared by everyone." There are well-established economic and political frameworks for understanding such commons, emerging from the history of agricultural common lands found in places like preindustrial England. This article provides a primer on the history and these frameworks, and considers a key difference between the information commons and the fields of yore: while information commons are robust and immensely valuable --- some can be said to rank among humanity's greatest achievements --- the English agricultural commons no longer meaningfully exist. The latter are gone not because of the well-known "tragedy of the commons," but rather a phenomenon known as the enclosure movement (~1600--1800) that transformed the common lands into private property. Many observers, then and now, judge enclosure to have been theft at a societal scale. This article argues that artificial intelligence (AI) provides precisely the tools needed to enable a previously-infeasible enclosure of the information commons. Although AI-enabled enclosure does not operate identically to physical enclosure, it shares the key features of turning the commons into private wealth and undermining the social systems that support them (via "slop spam"). The concepts presented in this article can provide a scholarly basis for interrogating the foreboding feeling that AI may represent not just a smash-and-grab, but an attack upon a whole way of life. title: Most Americans Say AI Is Bad for Society, Oppose More Data Centers
abstract:
Most Americans say AI is bad for society, oppose more data centers: ABC/Post/Ipsos poll Majorities see risks in AI and fewer see benefits. By Emily Guskin October 21, 2026, 6:09 AM A majority of Americans say artificial intelligence is a bad thing for society and about two-thirds oppose the construction of new data centers in the U.S., with opposition even higher to building data centers in people's own communities, according to an ABC News/Washington Post/Ipsos poll conducted using Ipsos’ KnowledgePanel . The poll finds that a 57% majority of Americans say AI is bad for society while 42% say it is good for society. Just 2% say it is "extremely" good for society while 17% say it is extremely bad for society. Related President Donald Trump announces creation of 'Super Intelligence Force' AI task force Tech leaders have issued warnings about the threat of AI and called for steps to slow it down before it outsmarts humans. Following those warnings, lawmakers have weighed what -- if any -- action should be taken. President Donald Trump, who has called warnings about AI a "hoax, " met with several tech leaders at the White House last month , saying they signed a "constitution" to police themselves. President Donald Trump speaks alongside Mark Zuckerberg, CEO of Meta Platforms, Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla and SpaceX, Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, Speaker of the House Mike Johnson and others holds a press briefing with AI executives following a meeting on artificial intelligence outside the West Wing of the White House, Sept. 29, 2026. Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images Younger Americans are more likely to say AI is bad for society than older Americans: 65% of Americans under 30 say AI is bad for society along with 59% of those 30 to 39. A slimmer majority of Americans 40 and older say AI is bad for society (53%). Majorities of Democrats (63%) and independents (58%) say AI is bad for society, while Republicans are more evenly split with 51% saying AI is good for society and 47% saying it is bad for society. Still, Americans are more likely to say AI is good for them personally: 50% say AI is good for them and 49% say it is bad for them. Again, intensity lies with the pessimists. Five times as many people say it is extremely bad for them (15%) compared to extremely good (3%). A majority of Republicans (57%) say AI is personally good for them while a similar majority of Democrats say it’s personally bad for them (55%). Independents are split on whether AI is good (50%) or bad (49%) for them personally. Risks and benefits of AI When Americans were asked about various potential risks with the growth of AI, majorities say that most of the possible consequences are a "high risk." Nearly three-quarters of Americans, 73%, say there is a high risk of AI hacking secure computer systems, including majorities across partisan groups and age groups. About two-thirds of Americans, 65%, say there is a high risk of the growth of AI leading to the elimination of many jobs, including majorities across age, partisan and income groups. About 6 in 10 Americans, 62%, say there is a high risk of people losing the ability to make their own decisions without AI, including a larger majority of Americans under the age of 50 (67%). Majorities across partisan groups say there’s a high risk of people losing the ability to make their own decisions without AI: 68% of Democrats, 63% of independents and 55% of Republicans. More than half of Americans, 54%, say there is a high risk of increasing economic inequality due to the growth of AI, including most Democrats (66%) and independents (57%) and just over a third of Republicans (36%). Similar majorities across income levels say there’s a high risk of increased economic inequality with the growth of AI. Related About 6 in 10 Americans are confident the election will be conducted fairly and accurately: ABC/Post/Ipsos poll One-third of Americans, 33%, say there is a high risk of human extinction due to the growth of AI -- a smaller share than the other risks, but for the most dire of consequences. Democrats are more likely to say that the growth of AI will lead to a high risk of human extinction (40%) than Republicans (24%), with independents falling in between (34%). When it comes to the potential benefits of AI, smaller shares of Americans say there's a big chance of each happening -- although roughly the same share say there's a big chance of AI making everyday tasks easier as say that there is a high risk of human extinction due to AI. About one-third of Americans, 34%, say that the growth of AI has a big chance of making everyday tasks easier. That includes a larger share of Republicans (42%) than independents (33%) or Democrats (29%). Three in 10 Americans (30%) say that the growth of AI has a big chance of leading to U.S. dominance in AI technology, including more Republicans (41%) than independents (27%) or Democrats (25%). Just 2 in 10 Americans (20%) say that the growth of AI has a big chance of making people more productive, including relatively small minorities across demographic groups; nearly twice as many say there is "little or no chance" of AI making people more productive (38%). Related 'Let Data Reign': Trump goes all in on controversial data centers And even fewer, 13% of Americans, say that the growth of AI has a big chance of creating many new jobs -- just over half, 52%, say it has little or no chance of creating many new jobs. More Republicans (17%) than Democrats (9%) say that AI has a big chance of creating many new jobs, but even the share of Republicans saying this is quite small. Most Democrats (60%) and independents (54%) along with 42% of Republicans say AI has little or no chance of creating many new jobs. Regulation and the administration Two-thirds of Americans say the federal government is not doing enough to regulate the growth and development of AI technology, including majorities of Democrats (80%), independents (66%) and Republicans (54%). Just 22% of Americans say the government is doing "about the right amount" to regulate AI. Two-thirds of Americans disapprove of how Trump is handling AI; just 30% approve. Approval peaks among MAGA Republicans -- who make up about 6 in 10 Republicans -- 80% of whom approve. But approval falls to 49% among non-MAGA Republicans, 50% of whom disapprove. Wide majorities of Democrats (92%) and independents (75%) disapprove of how Trump is handling AI. Urgent security fix issued for code vital to estimated 70% of all websites 2 days ago Retired detective charged in possible road rage killing on George Washington Bridge 2 days ago What workplace violence perpetrators have in common, new Secret Service report finds Oct 21 Americans trust Democrats over Republicans to handle AI, 26% to 19%, but about half say they don’t trust either party to handle AI (49%). In April, Americans were roughly split over trusting Democrats or Republicans more, with still about half saying they didn’t trust either party. Building data centers Two-thirds of Americans (66%) oppose the construction of new data centers in the U.S., growing to 72% when asked about building a new data center in their community. Data centers are a key issue ahead of high-stakes midterm elections. Trump has stressed his strong support for them , saying they can help enrich communities and assist in the United States’ effort to defeat China in the global AI race. Majorities across partisan groups and virtually all other major demographic groups oppose a new data center in their community. That includes 81% of Democrats, 76% of independents and 58% of Republicans, along with 80% of adults under 30 and 69% of those 65 or older. An aerial view of the 5C Data Centers CMH01, Oct. 18, 2026, in Springfield, Ohio. Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images Opposition is slightly higher in rural communities (78%), but 72% of suburbanites agree, along with 69% of urbanites, who are much less likely to face data center construction in their own backyards.

title: AI analysis of CT scans finds 42.9% of patients have coronary inflammation
abstract:
Oct 22, 2026 Biograph completes first U.S. study with Caristo Diagnostics’ AI-Powered Coronary Inflammation Detection, finding risk in over 42% of asymptomatic patients Biograph completes first U.S. study with Caristo Diagnostics’ AI-Powered Coronary Inflammation Detection, finding risk in over 42% of asymptomatic patients The study evaluated whether AI analysis of coronary inflammation in cardiac CT scans can help identify early cardiovascular risk before symptoms or obstructive plaque appear The study evaluated whether AI analysis of coronary inflammation in cardiac CT scans can help identify early cardiovascular risk before symptoms or obstructive plaque appear Press Release Biograph, the world’s most advanced preventive health and diagnostics clinic, today announced the completion of its first U.S. study using Caristo Diagnostics’ CaRi-Heart® technology evaluating AI-powered coronary inflammation detection in asymptomatic, low-risk individuals. The research revealed that coronary inflammation is widespread among asymptomatic adults without known heart disease – and is undetected by standard blood tests and other traditional cardiovascular risk factors. The study, available to clinically eligible Biograph Black tier members, combined Biograph’s advanced diagnostics – including high-resolution coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) imaging and cardiometabolic profiling – with Caristo’s CaRi-Heart and CaRi-Plaque ® technologies*. This collaborative methodology enabled researchers to assess the prevalence of coronary inflammation using the AI-enabled CaRi-Heart technology to determine cardiovascular risk in individuals who may otherwise appear low risk through traditional screening. The study found that coronary inflammation is common (42.9%) in asymptomatic, low-risk adults and frequently occurs without any plaque buildup or blockage. Specifically, 42.9% of participants exhibited elevated inflammation with 17.9% of participants exhibiting very high inflammation in at least one major heart artery. The results also suggest a potential limitation in standard assessment: About 47% of participants with no detectable coronary plaque exhibited elevated coronary perivascular inflammation. By evaluating coronary inflammation alongside traditional imaging assessment of plaque burden and stenosis, we get a more complete picture of cardiovascular risk.. Importantly, routine bloodwork and clinical tools – including cholesterol markers (ApoB, non-HDL-C), blood sugar (HbA1c), systemic inflammation (hs-CRP), and a widely used cardiovascular risk calculator (AHA PREVENT-ASCVD) – showed no correlation with the presence of coronary inflammation and failed to identify which patients had inflamed arteries. These results reinforce Biograph’s core philosophy: standalone bloodwork and isolated metrics do not tell the full story. By directly analyzing the biology of the tissue surrounding the coronary arteries, this non-invasive AI technology uncovers potential cardiovascular risk years before the onset of irreversible heart disease. "Coronary heart disease, whether plaque accumulation or arterial stenosis, is likely a late consequence of an active inflammatory process in the vessel wall. What is striking about our findings is that more than 42% of asymptomatic, conventionally low-risk adults had elevated coronary inflammation, and many individuals with the highest inflammatory levels had completely normal coronary anatomy on CT. Crucially, no routine blood biomarker, lipid metric, or clinical risk score could identify these individuals with inflamed coronary arteries. This study suggests we may be identifying an upstream phase of disease and a window for proactive intervention. More research is needed to validate this finding and establish the prognostic value and benefit of care directed at coronary perivascular inflammation." Michael Doney, MD, MPH, MS Executive Medical Director of Biograph Michael Doney, MD, MPH, MS Executive Medical Director of Biograph For Biograph, the completion of this study reflects its broader mission to advance proactive, personalized healthcare through comprehensive diagnostics, clinical interpretation, and earlier insight into long-term health risks. To review the clinical study manuscript, readers can access the published preprint here. *CaRi-Heart® has received U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) De Novo marketing authorization and is the first and only solution to quantify coronary inflammation from routine coronary CT angiography (CCTA). CaRi-Plaque® has received U.S. FDA clearance for AI-assisted coronary plaque and stenosis analysis, complementing CaRi-Heart by evaluating quantitative plaque. title: Award-winning AI literature
abstract:
Award-Winning AI Literature This a list of literary awards granted to works where AI was used (or was suspected) as part of the writing process AI WAS ALLOWED FROM THE START 🇯🇵 Short story Are You There? by Kamome Ashizawa — 9th Nikkei Hoshi Shinichi Literary Award, Excellence Award, 2022 Ashizawa made 101 stories in three weeks with AI. The story that won was mostly written by Ashizawa with a little AI; the other hundred experiments were mostly machine-generated. This was the first AI-assisted story to win a Hoshi prize. 🇯🇵 Short story The Last Painter by Toh Katagiri — 12th Nikkei Hoshi Shinichi Literary Award, Excellence Award, 2025 The organizers classified it as AI-assisted, but never said exactly how. A fellow finalist says Katagiri told the group that every sentence was written personally. 🇯🇵 Short story Genome Tower by Shamizui — 13th Nikkei Hoshi Shinichi Literary Award, Grand Prix, 2026 The disclosed AI use was apparently limited to inventing the name of a fictional disease. The organizers still counted it among the year’s AI-assisted winners. 🇯🇵 Short story Parallel Self-Mediation Co., Ltd. by En Shijima — 13th Nikkei Hoshi Shinichi Literary Award, Excellence Award, 2026 Shijima described working with AI as feeling more like “choosing” than “writing.” This sounds like a much more generative collaboration than Genome Tower . The prize stood. 🇯🇵 Short story Erinnerung by Rino Takinouchi — 13th Nikkei Hoshi Shinichi Literary Award, Excellence Award, 2026 ChatGPT produced initial material. Takinouchi corrected confused pronouns, dated phrases, and broken logic, then changed the title and ending and added the CRISPR-Cas9 material. Of the 2026 Hoshi winners, this has the clearest public account of AI-generated prose being extensively rewritten. The 13th Hoshi award received 2,107 entries. Organizers counted 491 as partly AI-created and said three of the four general-division winners had used AI somewhere in the process. 🇺🇸 Artist books The Library of Nonhuman Books by Karen Ann Donnachie and Andy Simionato — Robert Coover Award, First Place, 2020 An AI reading machine uses computer vision, OCR, and language processing to find short poetic combinations in physical books, erase the surrounding words, pair them with images, and publish new volumes. One of those volumes, Perception , also won Australia’s Cornish Family Prize. 🇸🇰 Poetry collection Výsledky vzniku by Liza Gennart — Zlatá vlna, 2021 Zuzana Husárová and Ľubomír Panák trained GPT-2 on 2,108 Slovak works, then curated and lightly edited its poems. The collection won Slovakia’s annual prize for the best original Slovak poetry book. 🇺🇸 Poetry series ReRites by David Jhave Johnston — Electronic Literature Organization Robert Coover Award, 2022 Twelve books of poetry built from neural-network output selected and edited by Johnston. The project openly calls itself “Human + A.I. poetry,” which is exactly the kind of thing an electronic-literature award exists to recognize. 🇺🇸 Chapbook A Black Story May Contain Sensitive Content by Lillian-Yvonne Bertram — DIAGRAM/New Michigan Press Chapbook Contest, Winner, 2023 Bertram used GPT-3 and Warpland, a model trained on Gwendolyn Brooks. Three sections contain machine responses to her prompts. The press knew how the book was made and published it openly. 🇺🇸 Short story Stargazers by Ruei-Jie Chang — UCSB Mind & Machine Intelligence Writing Contest, First Prize, 2024 Chang used ChatGPT for the seed of the story and Claude to organize and translate a Mandarin-English draft, then revised it. The contest explicitly welcomed human-only, machine-only, and hybrid entries, and required everyone to document the process. 🇷🇺 Short story 30–70 by Yana Vagner — Valentin Kataev Literary Prize, Winner, 2025 Vagner wrote the story with Alice, Yandex’s AI assistant. It begins by showing her prompt and the AI’s response, then uses the system for recurring climate reports. The collaboration was visible when the story won. 🇬🇧 Generative poem WORDS BEYOND WORDS by Sasha Stiles — Lumen Prize Literature & Poetry Award, 2025 A fine-tuned language model uses Stiles’s prompts, source texts, and code to make a new poem whenever the work is refreshed. The system itself, rather than a single fixed output, received the award. 🇬🇧 Interactive fiction Flesh & Blood by Chris Joseph — Electronic Literature Organization Robert Coover Award, 2026 An interactive story where readers solve puzzles in a disturbing world of bodies and machinery. Joseph openly lists it among his AI-assisted works . ORGANIZERS OR PUBLISHERS SAID AI WAS USED 🇫🇷 Novel C’était ça ou mourir by Thélyson Orélien — Prix du Roman Fnac, 2026 The novel won Fnac’s prize, then was removed from the Goncourt longlist after AI allegations. On October 21, Boréal dropped Orélien after an external review reportedly found AI markers in working-document metadata. The publisher said it still did not know how much AI had been used. Orélien had denied that any sentence was machine-generated. 🇸🇬 Poems Migrant Writers of Singapore poetry competition — Migrant Literature Festival, 2024 Eight winners were announced, then the entire list was recalled after organizers said three winning entries were AI-generated. Their review relied partly on Scribbr and QuillBot. 🇺🇸 Poems Poetry.com November and December contests — Two Monthly First Prizes, 2024 Poetry.com said both original winners were created “with assistance” from AI, changed the results, and redistributed the prizes. The removed poems and writers are no longer reliably identifiable. The names on the current result pages are the replacements, not the accused entrants. CONFIRMED AI USE 🇯🇵 Novel Sympathy Tower Tokyo by Rie Kudan — 170th Akutagawa Prize, 2024 Kudan first guessed that about 5% of the novel involved ChatGPT, then gave a much smaller figure: about one page out of 143. She consulted its output for the replies written by the AI inside the novel. The prize stood. 🇨🇳 Short story The Land of Machine Memories by Shen Yang, writing as “QuartZen” — 5th Youth Popular Science and Science Fiction Competition, Second Prize, 2023 AI generated the title, prose, illustrations, and pen name over 66 rounds of prompting. The organizer invited Shen and hid the experiment from the judges. This is often called a national literary prize, but it was a broad Jiangsu association contest: 18 stories shared second prize and 90 of roughly 200 entries received awards. 🇯🇵 Web novel Modest Skill “Tidying Up” Is the Strongest! — 18th AlphaPolis Fantasy Novel Awards, Grand Prize and Reader’s Choice, 2025 The author said a large majority of the web novel was made with generative AI. AlphaPolis later canceled the print edition and manga adaptation and changed its rules. Reporting confirms those cancellations, but not that the two award labels were formally revoked. 🇺🇸 Memoir How to Win One Million Dollars and $#!T Glitter! by Luke Stoffel — IBPA Book Award, Benjamin Franklin Silver Medal for Neurodivergent Communities, 2026 Stoffel says he used ChatGPT for grammar and structural scaffolding and disclosed it in the book and award submission. IBPA’s guidelines did not prohibit AI-assisted work , and the book received Silver. IBPA has not publicly commented on his AI use. SUSPECTED OR DISPUTED 🇿🇼 Short story The Blue Fighter by Simbarashe Steyn Kundizeza — Caine Prize for African Writing, Winner, 2026 Pangram flagged almost the entire story as AI-generated, according to The Atlantic . Kundizeza denied using AI and said the story drew on his family’s experiences. The prize opened a review. No final finding or revocation had been announced as of October 21. 🇬🇧 Short story The Serpent in the Grove by Jamir Nazir — Commonwealth Short Story Prize, Overall Winner, 2026 Pangram called it 100% AI-generated. Nazir denied it and described six or seven drafts made with Android speech-to-text because of a chronic condition.

title: Show HN: We had AI write a wiki from 45k Enron emails, every fact cited
abstract:
We built Enron a company brain We gave an AI 45,047 of Enron's emails, and it wrote 214 pages about the companies, regulators and banks Enron dealt with. Every fact cites the email it came from. When the mail shows a fact stopped being true, the page expires it on that date. No one edited a page or a fact. Explore Dynegy → How we did it The last two come from a held-out audit by a second AI; see how we checked it . These are the most-discussed organizations in the corpus. Each page has a slider. Drag it and the page shows what was known on that date, with facts that were only true for a while expiring in front of you. Facts on these pages are sentences, each with a date and a source, rather than fields like headcount or revenue. Fields belong in a CRM or another system of record, and a brain like this one sits beside it, holding what changes too often or doesn't fit in a field. We describe the three kinds of company knowledge, and where each one lives, in The missing middle of company knowledge . The pipeline proposed 57 narrow types and a person kept 54 of them. Almost all were kinds of organization, so we group these lists by a coarser class and keep the pipeline's own type as a tag on each entity. Companies, regulators, law firms, banks, newspapers. What the company deals with. Enron's own business units, desks, platforms, systems and codenamed projects. The pipeline also found 78 products and platforms , 76 facilities and market points , and 49 events , listed without pages. Choosing which kinds of entity deserve a page is the setup a person does when configuring a company brain, and we made that choice before building any page. Every company's mail names things it doesn't need to track, in categories that are a bit of a mess: restaurants from catered events, airports from travel, movies mentioned in passing. Enron's mail is no different. The facilities include trading hubs, Enron Field, a parking garage and two tankers. The events mix business conferences with charity bike rides and Cirque du Soleil. The products mix software with an exchange, a statute and trade associations. The right choice depends on the company. An event company should have pages for its events, a property manager for its facilities, and a hardware maker for its products. For Enron we gave pages to organizations named in at least 25 messages, and to the five most-discussed parts of Enron itself: three business units, a trading platform and a trading system. A real company brain wouldn't filter by count. A customer you signed today might have sent one or two emails, and you'd still want its page. The cutoff stands in for the judgment a person makes about what's worth keeping in the brain. We're this+that . We made these pages with a prototype of something we're building. We wanted a corpus anyone can check our work against. Enron's mail is public because the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) released it during its investigation, and Carnegie Mellon has maintained it since 2003. It's a large, free and widely used body of a real company's internal correspondence. The company's history is also settled, so a page claiming, for example, that Dynegy agreed to acquire Enron in November 2001 can be checked against the record rather than taken on trust. The mail shows the story in pieces. For the whole of it, read The Smartest Guys in the Room by Bethany McLean and Peter Elkind, who covered Enron's rise and fall as senior writers at Fortune.

title: UN says breaching 1.5C warming limit is 'imminent and unavoidable'
abstract:
A wind turbine generates electricity at sunset in Balabanli, near Tekirdag, Turkey, on Friday, Oct. 9. Emrah Gurel/AP Climate change People in entertainment Air quality Pollution See all topics Follow A UN climate report released Wednesday finds the globe will unavoidably slip past the Paris Climate Agreement’s 1.5-degree Celsius warming target in the next few years. The task now, the report states, is to make the period of warming “overshoot” as limited as possible, eventually bringing global average temperatures back down. The annual UN Emissions Gap report is designed to inform decision makers headed into the next round of global climate talks in Turkey, known as COP31, next month. While past gap reports have expressed skepticism about meeting the 1.5-degree target, this one marks the first time that its authors have pronounced that missing the mark will be “imminent and unavoidable.” “We are now saying this window has closed, but we can open it again by making the overshoot as brief as possible,” UN Environment Program Executive Director Inger Andersen said on a call with reporters. “This is about how to find a way back as shortly and as quickly as possible with as limited an overshoot as possible.” Go beyond the forecast with stunning stories and visuals. Download CNN Weather Past reports have examined the distance between countries’ emissions reduction commitments and what it would take to limit global warming to 1.5 C above preindustrial levels. However, this year’s report redefines the gap. Instead, it examines new emissions overshoot scenarios, and what it would take to limit peak warming to just 1.7 to 1.8 degrees C before bringing temperatures back down to 1.5 C through emissions cuts and the use of carbon removal technologies. The report makes clear that every additional fraction of a degree of warming above 1.5 C “raises the risk of irreversible changes including in ice sheets, permafrost carbon, ocean circulation, and coral systems, along with devastating human impacts.” Each added fraction of a degree of warming can have an “immense” impact “as measured in terms of damage, cost and loss of lives,” said climate scientist Michael Mann of the University of Pennsylvania. Mann was not involved in producing the UNEP report. The LPG and chemical tanker Bertolle sails through the Bosporus in Istanbul, Turkey, on Wednesday, Oct. 7. Emrah Gurel/AP No upbeat scenario for overshoot According to the UNEP, which is based in Nairobi, the lowest overshoot scenario would keep peak warming to between 1.7 and 1.8 degrees C and return global average temperatures to at or below 1.5 C by 2100. However, to follow such a pathway, global greenhouse gas emissions would need to be slashed by far more than anything currently on the table at the upcoming COP31 talks. This would require an 18% cut by 2030, 45% by 2035, and 69% by 2040, relative to 2025 levels. Meeting this lowest-possible overshoot scenario would require a tripling of renewable electricity capacity by 2035, and dramatic cuts to fossil fuels, including the phaseout of coal by 2040, the report states. ⛅ Get CNN Weather in your inbox The forecast is just the beginning. We’ll send you expert coverage and the stories behind the weather — so you always know more than just the number. Sign up for the newsletter In addition, there would need to be a major scaling up of carbon removal technologies, which so far have not been proven to work at such a large scale. In stark contrast to these figures, the fulfillment of existing emissions reduction pledges would only yield a 5-to-8% emissions cut by 2030 and an 11-to-15% reduction by 2035, the report found. This would be associated with a peak warming of about 2.6 degrees C. If countries simply follow their current policies, then warming could reach a peak of about 2.8 C. That estimate has increased since last year, in part because of the withdrawal of the United States from the Paris Agreement and retraction of its emissions reduction commitments, the report states. Even the scenario that assumes countries meet their existing reduction commitments, and nations with net-zero pledges succeed in fulfilling them, still brings warming to a peak of 2.1 C. Children look out of a window as a gas flare burns at the Cardon refinery in Punta Cardon, Venezuela, May 6. Gaby Oraa/Reuters/File The bottom line Clearly, overshooting 1.5 degrees C by the most limited amount possible and then coaxing temperatures back down over time is a tall order compared to what countries have pledged to do so far. “Without urgent action, the lowest possible 1.5 C overshoot pathway will quickly fade,” the report warns. “Every five years of CO2 emissions at current levels pushes peak warming up by around 0.1 C.” Mann said an additional 0.1 C of global warming “Permanently cuts global GDP by roughly 1.2% (over $1.2 trillion annually) and pushes approximately 140 million more people into life-threatening, dangerously hot climates.” Overshooting the 1.5-degree target can be viewed as a milestone, but it doesn’t mean an absolute failure of climate science and policy, according to climate scientist Kate Marvel of Project Drawdown, a climate research and solutions nonprofit. Marvel was not involved in the UNEP report. “There’s nothing special about any given temperature threshold,” she said. “The right unit isn’t degrees, it’s tons — of carbon dioxide, methane and other greenhouse gases. If we want to avoid the worst impacts, our task is and has always been to reduce these emissions as quickly as possible.” “Passing 1.5 degrees is a sign that we’re not moving fast enough, but it doesn’t mean we’re doomed,” she said . title: Swedish government offices to ban ChatGPT and Claude
abstract:

Foto: Kiichiro Sato/AP AI-SÄKERHET Regeringskansliet spärrar AI-tjänsterna Chat GPT och Claude 2 MIN Publicerad Idag 12:20 · 2:08 min Regeringskansliet inför en spärr för AI-tjänsterna Chat GPT och Claude, som från måndag inte längre kan nås från personalens tjänstedatorer. Spärren införs för att man vill att medarbetarna använder de tjänster som regeringskansliet godkänt, däribland Microsofts AI-verktyg Copilot. Samtidigt har man efter en översyn också höjt säkerheten i Copilot, vilket framkommer av intern information som Ekot har tagit del av. Digitaliseringsdirektör Mikael Wettercrantz har avböjt en intervju med Ekot men säger i en kommentar på Regeringskansliets intranät, att användning av AI-tjänster utan avtal kan få ”konsekvenser för vår informationssäkerhet”. Ekots kartläggning visar att Regeringskansliet inte är ensamma. Spärrar har införts både på Skatteverket och Statens institutionsstyrelse, Sis, och hos Kronofogden bereds frågan just nu inför ett kommande ställningstagande. ”Problematisk användning” Riskerna med oreglerad AI-användning har uppmärksammats inom en rad myndigheter där man också haft skäl att vidta andra åtgärder. Bland annat Trafikverket, där internrevisionen tidigare i år upptäckte en utbredd och riskfylld användning av ett tiotal olika AI-tjänster och skrev så här: ”Vi har tagit del av flera exempel på problematisk användning av öppna AI-tjänster. Exemplen rör både känsligheten i den information som matats in och hur de AI-genererade svaren hanterats” Höjt säkerhet i Copilot På Regeringskansliet har man sedan tidigare begränsat användningen av AI-tjänsten Deepseek. Samtidigt uppger presstjänsten att en del av personalen kommer att ha fortsatt tillgång till en särskild plattform för AI-assistenter som Regeringskansliet själva utvecklat, och genom vilken man får tillgång till ChatGPT och Claude. Av den interna informationen framgår också att man efter en översyn valt att höja säkerheten i det godkända verktyget Copilot, men presstjänsten vill inte gå in på några detaljer om den skärpningen, med hänvisning till att den handlar om säkerhetsfrågor.
